according to.definition: As said or shown by someone or something.
according to.example: According to the news, the road is closed.

act on.definition: To do something because of advice, information or a feeling.
act on.example: She acted on her doctor's advice.

add up.definition: To increase gradually until it becomes a large amount.

after all.definition: Used to give a reason; or to say something happened despite what was expected.
after all.example: Let him sleep. After all, he's only a baby.

ahead of.definition: In front of; or before someone else.
ahead of.example: They launched the product ahead of their rivals.

all in all.definition: Used to give a general opinion after thinking about everything.
all in all.example: All in all, it was a great holiday.

all of a sudden.example: All of a sudden, the lights went out.

allow in.definition: To let someone enter a place.

allow out.definition: To let someone go outside or leave.
allow out.example: The kids aren't allowed out after dark.

any more.definition: Used in negatives to say something has stopped.
any more.example: I don't live there any more.

apart from.definition: Except for; or as well as.

as a result.example: He didn't study. As a result, he failed.

as if.definition: In a way that suggests something, often something not true.
as if.example: He talks as if he knows everything.

as long as.example: You can borrow it as long as you bring it back.

as soon as.example: Call me as soon as you get home.

as though.definition: As if; in a way that suggests something.
as though.example: She looked as though she hadn't slept.

as usual.definition: In the way that happens most of the time.

as well as.example: She speaks French as well as English.

at all.definition: Used in negatives and questions to make them stronger.
at all.example: I didn't sleep at all last night.

at first.definition: At the beginning, before something changed.
at first.example: At first I didn't like him, but now we're friends.

at least.definition: Not less than; or used to add something positive.
at least.example: It will take at least an hour.

at once.definition: Immediately; or at the same time.

at the end of the day.definition: Used to say what is most important after thinking about everything.
at the end of the day.example: At the end of the day, it's your decision.

because of.definition: As a result of; for the reason of.
because of.example: We stayed inside because of the storm.

break down.definition: When a machine or car stops working.
break down.example: Our car broke down on the motorway.

break in.definition: To enter a building by force, usually to steal.
break in.example: Someone broke in and took the TV.

break up.example: They broke up after two years.

bring in.example: The school brought in a new rule.

bring up.definition: To care for a child until they are an adult.
bring up.example: She was brought up by her grandparents.

build on.definition: To use something as a base to develop further.
build on.example: We can build on last year's success.

by accident.example: I deleted the file by accident.

by far.definition: By a very large amount; used with superlatives.
by far.example: She is by far the best student in the class.

by the time.definition: Not later than the moment when something happens.
by the time.example: By the time we arrived, the film had started.

by the way.definition: Used to add a new topic or extra information.
by the way.example: By the way, have you seen Anna?

call back.definition: To phone someone again, or phone someone who called you.
call back.example: I'll call you back in ten minutes.

call up.example: I called him up to say sorry.

carry out.definition: To do a task, plan or piece of research.
carry out.example: They carried out a survey of students.

carry over.definition: To continue into a new situation or part.
carry over.example: The subject carries over from the first clause.

catch up.definition: To reach someone who is ahead; or to do work you have not done yet.
catch up.example: I have to catch up on my homework.

check out.definition: To go and look at something interesting.
check out.example: You should check out the new café.

clean up.definition: To make a place completely clean and tidy.
clean up.example: We cleaned up after the party.

close to.example: Our flat is close to the station.

come along.example: We're going to the park — come along!

come down.definition: In 'when it comes down to it': when you think about what really matters.
come down.example: When it comes down to it, family is everything.

come in.definition: To enter a room or building.

come on.definition: Used to encourage someone or to show you don't believe them.

come out.example: Her new book comes out next week.

come over.definition: To visit someone at their home.
come over.example: Come over on Saturday for lunch.

come up.definition: To happen or appear, often unexpectedly.
come up.example: Something came up, so I can't come.

come up with.definition: To think of an idea or plan.
come up with.example: She came up with a great idea.

cut down.definition: In 'cut down on': to do or use less of something.
cut down.example: I'm trying to cut down on sugar.

decide on.example: Have you decided on a name?

die out.example: Many old traditions have died out.

drop by.definition: To visit someone for a short time without planning.
drop by.example: Drop by if you're in the area.

due to.example: The match was cancelled due to rain.

each other.definition: Used to show that each of two or more people does the same thing to the other.
each other.example: Anna and Tom help each other with homework.

end up.definition: To be in a situation you did not plan.
end up.example: We ended up staying at home.

even though.definition: Although; used to show a surprising contrast.
even though.example: She went out even though it was raining.

face up.definition: In 'face up to': to accept and deal with a difficult situation.
face up.example: You need to face up to your problems.

fill in.definition: To write information on a form; or to tell someone the latest news.

fill out.definition: To write all the information on a form.

find out.definition: To learn a fact or discover information.
find out.example: I found out the truth yesterday.

first of all.definition: Used to introduce the first point or action.
first of all.example: First of all, thank you for coming.

fit in.definition: To feel comfortable and accepted in a group.
fit in.example: It took a while to fit in at my new school.

for a while.example: Let's sit here for a while.

for ages.example: I haven't seen her for ages.

for example.example: Many fruits, for example oranges, have vitamin C.

for good.example: They left the city for good.

get along.example: I get along well with my colleagues.

get in.definition: To enter a place, often with difficulty.
get in.example: The door was locked, but we got in.

get off.definition: To leave a bus, train or plane.
get off.example: Get off at the next stop.

get on.definition: To have a good relationship; or to enter a bus or train.
get on.example: I get on well with my brother.

get on with.definition: To have a friendly relationship with someone; or to continue doing something.
get on with.example: I get on with my sister very well.

get out.definition: To leave a place, often quickly.
get out.example: Everyone got out before the fire spread.

give away.definition: To give something to someone for free.
give away.example: She gave away all her old books.

give back.definition: To return something to its owner.
give back.example: Give me back my pen, please.

go along.definition: In 'go along with': to agree with or accept an idea.
go along.example: I'll go along with your plan.

go down.example: Prices have gone down this month.

go off.definition: When an alarm or bomb suddenly makes a noise or explodes.
go off.example: My alarm went off at six.

go on.example: The meeting went on for hours.

go out.definition: To leave home to do something social; or when a light stops shining.
go out.example: The lights went out during the storm.

grow up.definition: To change from a child into an adult.
grow up.example: I grew up in a small village.

hand in.definition: To give work to a teacher or person in charge.
hand in.example: Hand in your essays on Monday.

hand out.definition: To give something to each person in a group.
hand out.example: The teacher handed out the tests.

hang out.definition: To spend time relaxing with friends.
hang out.example: We usually hang out at the park.

help out.definition: To help someone, often with a practical job.
help out.example: Can you help out in the kitchen?

hurry up.example: Hurry up, or we'll miss the bus!

if only.definition: Used to say you strongly wish something were true or had happened.
if only.example: If only I had more free time!

in a hurry.definition: Needing or trying to do something quickly.

in a row.definition: One after another, without a break.
in a row.example: It rained for five days in a row.

in accordance with.definition: Following a rule, law or wish.
in accordance with.example: The work was done in accordance with the law.

in addition.definition: Also; used to add another point.
in addition.example: The flat is cheap. In addition, it's near the park.

in addition to.example: In addition to English, she speaks German.

in advance.definition: Before the time when something happens.

in case.example: Take an umbrella in case it rains.

in conclusion.definition: Used to start the last part of a speech or piece of writing.
in conclusion.example: In conclusion, zoos can help protect animals.

in fact.definition: Used to add something that is true, often surprising.
in fact.example: I don't mind. In fact, I'm quite happy.

in front of.definition: Close to the front part of something; facing it.
in front of.example: I'll meet you in front of the cinema.

in general.definition: Usually, or when thinking about something as a whole.
in general.example: In general, people here are very friendly.

in my opinion.definition: Used to say what you think.
in my opinion.example: In my opinion, the book is better than the film.

in order to.definition: With the purpose of doing something.
in order to.example: She saved money in order to buy a car.

in spite of.example: We enjoyed the trip in spite of the rain.

in terms of.definition: Used to say which aspect of something you mean.
in terms of.example: In terms of price, it's the best option.

in the end.definition: Finally, after a lot of changes or thought.
in the end.example: In the end, we stayed at home.

in the least.definition: Not at all; used in negatives for emphasis.
in the least.example: I wasn't in the least surprised.

in the meantime.definition: In the time between two events.
in the meantime.example: Dinner is at eight. In the meantime, relax.

instead of.definition: In the place of someone or something.
instead of.example: Let's walk instead of taking the bus.

join in.definition: To take part in an activity with others.

leave out.definition: To not include someone or something.

let in.definition: To allow someone to enter; in 'let someone in on': to tell them a secret.
let in.example: She let me in on a secret.

look down.definition: In 'look down on': to think you are better than someone.
look down.example: Don't look down on people with less money.

look forward to.definition: To feel happy and excited about something that is going to happen.
look forward to.example: I'm looking forward to the holidays.

look in.definition: To look into a place; or to visit someone briefly.
look in.example: He looked in and smiled at us.

look out.definition: In 'look out for': to watch carefully for someone or something.
look out.example: Look out for cars when you cross.

look up.definition: To find information in a dictionary or online.
look up.example: Look up the word in a dictionary.

look up to.example: I've always looked up to my grandfather.

lose touch.definition: To stop being in contact with someone.

make sure.definition: To check that something is true or will happen.
make sure.example: Make sure you lock the door.

make up.definition: In 'make up your mind': to decide.
make up.example: I can't make up my mind.

mark out.definition: To show that someone or something is different or special.
mark out.example: Her talent marked her out from the others.

mix up.definition: To think one thing or person is another.
mix up.example: I always mix up the twins.

more or less.example: The work is more or less finished.

move back.definition: To go back to an earlier position or place.
move back.example: They moved back to their home town.

move on.definition: To start doing or talking about something new.
move on.example: Let's move on to the next point.

narrow down.definition: To make a list or group smaller.
narrow down.example: We narrowed down the choice to two hotels.

next to.definition: Very close to; at the side of.
next to.example: The bank is next to the post office.

no matter.definition: Used to say that something is true in every case.
no matter.example: No matter what you say, I'll go.

not at all.definition: Used to say no strongly, or to reply politely to thanks.
not at all.example: Thanks for your help! — Not at all.

of course.definition: Used to say yes strongly, or that something is obvious.
of course.example: Of course you can borrow my bike.

on account of.definition: Because of; used in formal English.
on account of.example: The flight was delayed on account of fog.

on balance.definition: After thinking about all the facts.
on balance.example: On balance, I think the plan is good.

on purpose.example: Did you break it on purpose?

on the contrary.definition: Used to say that the opposite is true.
on the contrary.example: It wasn't boring. On the contrary, it was great.

on the other hand.definition: Used to introduce a different or opposite point.
on the other hand.example: It's cheap. On the other hand, it's very slow.

on the way.definition: During the journey to a place.
on the way.example: I'll buy bread on the way home.

on the whole.definition: Generally; when you think about everything.
on the whole.example: On the whole, I'm happy with my job.

on time.definition: At the planned time; not late.

out of nowhere.definition: Very suddenly and from an unknown place.
out of nowhere.example: A dog appeared out of nowhere.

pass down.definition: To give something to younger people in a family.
pass down.example: The ring was passed down from my grandmother.

pay attention.definition: To watch, listen or think about something carefully.
pay attention.example: Please pay attention to the instructions.

pick out.definition: To choose one thing from a group.
pick out.example: She picked out a red dress.

pick up.definition: To collect someone or something; or to lift something.
pick up.example: I'll pick you up at eight.

piece of cake.definition: Something that is very easy to do.
piece of cake.example: The test was a piece of cake.

point back.definition: To refer to something said or shown earlier.
point back.example: 'This' points back to the last sentence.

point out.definition: To tell someone about a fact they may not have noticed.
point out.example: She pointed out a mistake in my essay.

put down.definition: In 'put something down to': to say what caused it.
put down.example: He put his success down to hard work.

put off.definition: To move something to a later time.

put on.definition: To start wearing clothes; or to switch on.
put on.example: Put on your coat — it's cold.

put up.definition: To let someone stay in your home.
put up.example: My aunt put us up for a week.

put up with.definition: To accept something unpleasant without complaining.
put up with.example: I can't put up with this noise any longer.

rather than.example: I'd like tea rather than coffee.

rule out.definition: To decide that something is not possible.
rule out.example: The police ruled out an accident.

run out.definition: To be used until nothing is left.
run out.example: My phone battery has run out.

run out of.definition: To use all of something so there is none left.

scale up.definition: To make something bigger or stronger in degree.
scale up.example: We plan to scale up production.

sell out.definition: When all of something has been sold.
sell out.example: The tickets sold out in an hour.

set off.example: We set off early in the morning.

show up.example: He showed up an hour late.

sign in.definition: To write your name when you arrive, or to log in.

sign up.definition: To agree to take part in something by giving your name.
sign up.example: I signed up for a yoga class.

single out.definition: To choose one person or thing from a group for special attention.
single out.example: The teacher singled her out for praise.

sit down.definition: To move into a sitting position.

slot in.definition: To fit something into a space or position.
slot in.example: The new word slots in before the verb.

slow down.example: Slow down — you're driving too fast!

so far.example: So far, the trip has been great.

so that.definition: In order to make something possible.
so that.example: Speak loudly so that everyone can hear.

stand in.definition: To take someone's or something's place.
stand in.example: Can you stand in for me tomorrow?

stand out.definition: To be very easy to notice.
stand out.example: Her red coat stood out in the crowd.

stand up.example: Everyone stood up when she came in.

stay out.definition: To not come home, especially at night.

such as.example: I like fruit such as apples and pears.

sum up.definition: To give the main points of something briefly.
sum up.example: Let me sum up what we agreed.

swap around.definition: To change the positions of two things.
swap around.example: In questions, swap around the subject and verb.

switch off.definition: To stop a machine or light working.
switch off.example: Switch off the lights when you leave.

take care of.definition: To look after someone or something.
take care of.example: Can you take care of my cat this weekend?

take off.definition: When a plane leaves the ground; or to remove clothes.
take off.example: The plane took off on time.

take on.example: Don't take on too much work.

take out.definition: To remove something from a place.

take part.definition: To be involved in an activity with other people.
take part.example: Twenty teams took part in the competition.

take place.example: The concert will take place in the park.

take up.definition: To start a new hobby; in 'take someone up on': to accept an offer.

team up.definition: To join with someone to do something together.
team up.example: The two schools teamed up for the project.

thanks to.definition: Because of someone or something, usually something good.
thanks to.example: Thanks to your help, we finished early.

these days.example: These days, everyone has a smartphone.

think over.definition: To think carefully about something before deciding.
think over.example: Think it over and tell me tomorrow.

to begin with.definition: Used to give the first point; or at the start.
to begin with.example: To begin with, the tickets are too expensive.

to sum up.definition: Used before giving a short summary of what you have said.
to sum up.example: To sum up, both options have their good points.

trail off.definition: When speech gradually becomes quieter and stops.

try on.definition: To put on clothes to see if they fit.
try on.example: Can I try on these jeans?

turn around.definition: To change the order or direction of something.
turn around.example: You can turn the sentence around.

turn down.definition: To make sound or heat lower; or to refuse an offer.

turn off.definition: To stop a machine or light working.

turn on.definition: To start a machine or light working.

turn out.definition: To happen in a particular way, or be found to be true.
turn out.example: The film turned out to be great.

turn up.definition: To make sound or heat higher; or to arrive.
turn up.example: Turn up the heating — it's cold.

up to now.example: Up to now, we've had no problems.

use up.example: We've used up all the milk.

walk in.example: Everyone went quiet when he walked in.

wash up.definition: To wash the dishes after a meal.
wash up.example: I'll cook if you wash up.

what is more.definition: Used to add a more important point.
what is more.example: It's cheap, and what is more, it's very fast.

whether or not.definition: Used to say that something is true in either case.
whether or not.example: We'll go whether or not it rains.

uk.translation: чи ні; незалежно від того, чи

with regard to.example: I am writing with regard to your order.

work out.definition: To find the answer to a problem.
work out.example: I can't work out this puzzle.

work through.definition: To deal with something step by step until it is finished.
work through.example: We worked through the exercises together.

write down.definition: To write something on paper so you remember it.
